content:
For \(n\) near the target, include the \(625\) term.

\[
Z(n)=\left\lfloor\frac n5\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac n{25}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac n{125}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac n{625}\right\rfloor
\]

Check around \(n=1170\):

\[
Z(1169)=\left\lfloor\frac{1169}{5}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{1169}{25}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{1169}{125}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{1169}{625}\right\rfloor
=233+46+9+1=289
\]

\[
Z(1170)=234+46+9+1=290
\]

Therefore, the smallest \(n\) is

\[
\boxed{1170}
\]
